title: Wrap a read failure without losing its cause

blocks.text: Exception chaining wraps a caught exception inside another one before rethrowing it: the new exception adds context, and the original rides along as its **cause**, stack trace and all.

Write `ConfigLoader.load(Source source, String name)`. It returns `source.read(name)`. When the read throws an `IOException`, `load` throws a `ConfigException` (declared in the starter) whose message is `"Error processing file " + name`.
Whoever debugs the `ConfigException` later must still be able to reach the `IOException` that caused it. And wrap what the page calls a file-processing failure, nothing broader.

cases.says: It returns what the source reads.
An IOException becomes a ConfigException naming the file.
The original IOException is chained as the cause, so its stack trace survives.
Only the IOException is wrapped; an unchecked failure from the source reaches the caller as it is.

concepts: When an exception is wrapped and rethrown, the caught one is passed as the cause so its stack trace survives.
